title.value: Expressivity of Neural Networks with Random Weights and Learned Biases
title.justification: The title clearly outlines the focus of the paper, which is on understanding how neural networks express functions when having random weights and learned biases.
title.quote: E XPRESSIVITY OF N EURAL N ETWORKS WITH R ANDOM W EIGHTS AND L EARNED B IASES

analysis.description: The paper explores the theoretical and empirical aspects of neural networks that have fixed random weights and learned biases, specifically focusing on their ability to approximate any continuous function on compact sets. The work has relevance in both neuroscience, by suggesting ways neural changes can affect dynamics without weight modifications, and AI, by contributing to fine-tuning methods such as bias learning and prefix-based approaches for language models.

type.justification: The paper provides theoretical evidence and numerical experiments to support its claims about the expressivity of neural networks with random weights and learned biases.
type.quote: We provide theoretical and numerical evidence demonstrating that feedforward neural networks with fixed random weights can approximate any continuous function on compact sets.

name.justification: The main focus of the paper is on understanding and demonstrating the expressivity of neural networks when certain parameters (weights) are random and others (biases) are learned.
name.quote: Landmark universal function approximation results for neural networks with trained weights and biases provided the impetus for the ubiquitous use of neu- ral networks as learning models in neuroscience and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

name.justification: The paper examines the relevance of its findings to neuroscience by explaining how neural networks with bias learning can lead to behaviorally relevant dynamics.
name.quote: Our findings are relevant to neuroscience, where they demonstrate the potential for behaviorally relevant changes in dynamics without modifying synaptic weights,

name.justification: The paper discusses the application of its findings to AI, particularly in the context of modern sequence models such as transformers and fine-tuning methods.
name.quote: as well as for AI, where they shed light on recent fine-tuning methods for large language models, like bias and prefix-based approaches.

name.justification: The paper prominently discusses Feedforward Neural Networks with fixed random weights and learned biases as a model used to demonstrate their universal approximation capabilities.
name.quote: feedforward neural networks with fixed random weights can approximate any continuous function on compact sets.

is_contributed.justification: FNNs are used as part of the analysis rather than being an innovation or contribution of the paper.
is_contributed.quote: Our findings are relevant to neuroscience, where they demonstrate the potential for behaviourally relevant changes in dynamics without modifying synaptic weights, as well as for AI, where they shed light on recent fine-tuning methods for large language models, like bias and prefix-based approaches.

is_executed.justification: Numerical experiments were conducted with FNNs as part of the empirical exploration.
is_executed.quote: We further provide empirical support for, and a deeper interrogation of, these results with numerical experiments exploring multi-task learning, motor-control, and dynamical system forecasting.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares FNNs performance through numerical results, showcasing variations in learning with respect to parameters like random initialization.
is_compared.quote: We first validated the theory by checking whether a single-hidden-layer bias-learned FNN could perform classification on the Fashion MNIST dataset increasingly well as its hidden layer was widened.
